newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees CVRD pricing after study.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees CVRD pricing after study.

text.p: Brazil should be able to set the minimum price for the privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) after independent consultants complete a study on the value of new deposits, an official said.

Teresa Cristina Aquino, privatization superintendent at the National Development Bank (BNDES), said it was hoped consultants Mineral Research Development Inc (MRD) would have completed a probe of deposits at Carajas by February 6.
"Once we have their study we should be able to set the price," Aquino told Reuters, adding the Carajas assessment was the last remaining piece of the puzzle.
The CVRD sell-off was put back to April from the first quarter of 1997 following mounting speculation about a major gold and copper find at Carajas in Para state.
CVRD has carried out borings and says they are promising, but it is too early to evaluate the viability of the deposits.

Aquino said MRD's brief was to go over CVRD's results and audit them, as well as interview officials and technicians on site. The company would not have time to carry out any independent borings or take soil samples.
"We had an obligation to ask for an independent study, an obligation to the public," Aquino said.

Brazil's National Privatization Council postponed a January 29 meeting which had been due to discuss CVRD's base price. The next meeting is tentatively scheduled for February 6, but depends on whether MRD has completed its evaluation.
